title: JBS Hosts Local Colorado 4-H Students at Greeley Beef Facility to Celebrate National 4-H Week

body_markdown:
As part of National 4-H Week celebrations, JBS USA welcomed 4-H students from Weld County to our Greeley beef facility for an opportunity to connect with one of Northern Colorado's largest employers and learn about careers that help power the region's agricultural economy.


During the visit, students gained a behind-the-scenes look at how a modern beef processing facility operates while engaging directly with JBS team members about their career journeys. From engineering and food safety to logistics, operations and human resources, students learned how a variety of skills and interests can lead to rewarding careers within JBS and the broader agriculture industry.


The experience reinforced the important connection between agricultural education and workforce development, helping students explore future career pathways while building stronger ties between local 4-H programs, the agricultural community and one of the region's largest employers.


**Kim Eastwood, Weld County 4-H Extension:**
*“This was a valuable experience for our 4-H students. With JBS right here in their backyard, many of them are familiar with the company, but touring the facility gave them a firsthand look at an important part of the agricultural industry. Experiences like this strengthen the partnership between JBS and 4-H while helping students expand their agricultural education and explore future career opportunities.”*


**Denim Dutcher, Weld County 4-H Student:**
*"I've been interested in becoming a grader for a while, so it was fascinating to see firsthand how quality and consistency are evaluated throughout the process. The tour gave me a better understanding of what the job involves and what it takes to be successful."*


**Celio Fritche, President, JBS Beef USA:**
*"4-H has played an important role in developing generations of leaders in agriculture, and we're proud to support those efforts here in Colorado and across the country. Programs like this help students connect what they learn in the classroom and through 4-H with the real-world opportunities that exist throughout the food and agriculture industry. By opening our doors and sharing the work our team members do every day, we hope to inspire the next generation and help them see the many ways they can build meaningful careers while contributing to their communities."*


The tour highlighted the strength of the partnership between JBS and 4-H and a shared commitment to preparing the next generation of agricultural leaders. By providing students with firsthand exposure to careers in food production and introducing them to the people behind the work, JBS is helping young people see the many opportunities available to them within agriculture and beyond.
